incident.title: Inventory reservation processing slower for warehouse users
incident.alert_or_symptom: The Inventory Service remains available, but warehouse stock-reservation requests are processing more slowly than normal and a small proportion are timing out.

technical_evidence.observation: The p95 response time for stock-reservation requests increased from a normal baseline of 900 milliseconds to 4.8 seconds between 11:10 and 11:40.
Reservation throughput fell to 58 percent of the normal level. Of 8,240 reservation requests, 93.5 percent completed successfully and 6.5 percent timed out.
Health checks remained successful and inventory lookup, stock-view and adjustment functions continued to operate throughout the affected interval.
Thirty-eight warehouse users report slower stock reservations. Users can submit smaller reservation batches through the approved operating procedure, which is allowing priority orders to continue.

An Inventory Service reporting-library update was deployed approximately three hours before the degradation was detected. No evidence currently demonstrates that the update affected reservation processing.
No application exception, database failure, compute failure, network failure, dependency failure or configuration error has been directly identified.

service_impact.user_impact_description: Thirty-eight warehouse users are experiencing slower stock-reservation processing and occasional timeouts, while most requests and other inventory functions continue to succeed.
service_impact.business_function_affected: Warehouse stock reservation for order fulfilment
service_impact.workaround_description: Warehouse users can submit smaller reservation batches using the approved operating procedure, allowing priority orders to continue.

environmental_context: The Inventory Service is a Tier 2 important service.
Inventory lookup, stock-view and stock-adjustment functions remain available.
Customer ordering continues, and no incorrect stock value or data corruption has been confirmed.

recent_changes.description: A reporting-library update was deployed to the Inventory Service approximately three hours before the degradation was detected.

reported_unknowns: The directly responsible performance bottleneck has not been identified.
It is not known whether the recent reporting-library update is related to the degradation.
The current latency contribution and health of the Inventory Service dependencies have not been independently established.
The expected duration and recovery time are unknown.
additional_context: No complete service outage, data loss, corruption or serious security exposure has been reported.
The approved smaller-batch procedure is currently maintaining priority warehouse operations.
